newsitem.title: INDIA: Bombay shares end up, off lows as Rao case delayed.
newsitem.headline: Bombay shares end up, off lows as Rao case delayed.

text.p: Bombay shares ended down but off their lows as punters covered short positions after the criminal court postponed a hearing involving former prime minister P.V. Narasimha Rao until next week, traders said.
"The market was expecting some news on Rao's arrest and when it got delayed by a week, speculators ran to cover short positions," one trader said.

Rao's plea for protection against possible arrest was turned down last week. On Monday, the supreme court said it exempted the former PM from appearing in court on the same day due to security threats.
The benchmark Bombay stocks index closed 14.22 points lower at a provisional 3240.51, after hitting a late-session low of 3205.23.
Traders said most funds remained on the sidelines but some were sellers in blue chips including TELCO and MTNL.
Shares of State Bank of India were hammered to 248.25 in early trade on the Bombay Stock Exchange (BSE) before rebounding to end 1.25 rupees up at 252.75.
Traders said foreign funds were selling the underlying ahead of the firm's $400 million GDR issue.
They said it would be difficult for SBI to achieve its indicative pricing of 275 rupees in weak market conditions.
Petrochemicals firm Reliance told the BSE its board would meet on October 18 to approve 1996/97 first half results.
A Reuter poll of 14 leading securities houses last week found the petrochemical giant's first half net profit is headed for a 25.8 percent fall to 4.7 billion rupees from the year ago.

Shares of cable maker Sterlite fell 28.75 rupees to 185.75 ahead of results for the year ended June 30, 1996. The firm said its net climbed to 1.4 billion rupees after a merger with group firm Sterlite Communications. The merger -- effective from April 1 -- was passed by shareholders but is awaiting court approval.

Voting began in northern Uttar Pradesh state for crucial local assembly polls where Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda's United Front alliance takes on the Congress party and the BJP in a triangular fight.
